newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bank MFK Novolipetsk suit to be heard April 16.
newsitem.headline: Bank MFK Novolipetsk suit to be heard April 16.

text.p: A further hearing in a case against Novolipetsk Metals Combine about shareholder rights will be held on April 16, a spokesman for shareholders said on Friday.
Senior managers at Novolipetsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat were unavailable for comment on Friday afternoon.

Initial hearings of the case, in which Bank MFK argues plant management stripped it of its shareholder voting rights last year, were held earlier this week at Lipetsk Arbitration Court, the spokesman said.
Bank MFK, which is associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), one of Russia's biggest banks, holds 15 percent of Novolipetsk, which produced six million tonnes of steel in 1995.
Altogether the factory faces five separate lawsuits brought by state and private investors, as well as an investigation by the Russian Federal Securities Commission.

Hearings of suits brought by Cambridge Capital Management, a U.S. investment fund, and the Sputnik Fund, a branch of Renaissance Capital, claiming plant management refused to consider their nominees to the board of directors, are also scheduled for April 16.
"I guess the judges pushed it back so they can come to a comprehensive decision," said the spokesman.
A judge at Lipetsk Arbitration Court, who declined to be named, said earlier the case had been postponed until both sides had submitted further evidence.
